pr_body:
This commit fixes over-accounting recovered bytes when a file is recovered from a snapshot
and the connection between the source node and target node is closed. In that case the 
target keeps downloading the snapshot file and in some rare timings can lead to over-accounting
the number of recovered bytes. With this change when the recovery is restarted a new temporary
file prefix will be used, as well as a fresh `RecoveryState` avoiding collisions between the different
recovery phases.

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/90441
pr_title: Fix overcounting recovered bytes after network disconnect
pr_comment: Yes, I wanted to run CI first to see how many things break before opening the final PR.
I'll open a follow-up PR that cancels the snapshot file download when the connection is closed.
Hi @fcofdez, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

review_comment: Would it not be nicer to also return a new instance here? Would that be problematic?
For searchable snapshots we shouldn't run into this problem, we don't recover any file through regular recovery. So I figured that it should be fine to reuse the same instance.

To the reader however, it looks like this is either a micro-tuning (which seems unnecessary) or there is something special going on requiring us to not create a new state. I am fine to leave as is, but perhaps we can add a comment that it is equivalent to creating a new `SearchableSnapshotRecoveryState`?
I am not sure I see how we are sure this has not completed already before adding the request handling behavior?
Yes, that's a bit racy. I'll move it before we close the connections. Good catch.
